result.strongest_objection: R2 is a deliberate, quantified weakening of a fail-closed escape gate whose only mitigation is an explicitly unverified premise. Claim B / §6 R2 admit the design converts HEAD's per-run pass probability (1 − p) for an intermittent byte-altering relay into (1 − p³) — strictly weaker on the gate that exists (per the doc's own §3.1 rejection of direction (a)) precisely because World must not trust relay behavior. The mitigation offered is one sentence: 'No known srt path alters tunnel bytes… reasoned, not measured.' Yet the doc itself proves byte-prepending relays are in-scope (§3.2 names PROXY-protocol prepending; TC even pins that exact shape as foreign→retry), and row 230's ratified foreign-retry rule was for the reverse leg, where World is the dialer — it is not a ratified precedent for retrying escape-path accepts on the forward legs. Worst, the design's stated acceptance gate cannot see this class: the §7 CI step runs the honest srt path (CONNECT to 127.0.0.1 denied → empty window), and no test or V-row measures what the pinned srt proxy actually delivers upstream. A fail-closed gate's verdict path is being relaxed on an assertion the acceptance procedure never exercises.
result.catch: Verify, don't assert, the byte-fidelity premise — the srt install is pinned (ci.yml:226), so the executor or CI can grep the pinned srt source for the CONNECT/200 tunnel path and record verbatim-relay vs. any prepend/rewrite as a V-log row; absent that, the quorum must explicitly ratify the (1−p) → (1−p³) regression as an accepted weakening of arm 6. Also: r2's refactored code (shared readProbeLine/judgeLeg, renamed bound) is validated by a single −count=1 run (V17, load 1.17); the −count=3 stability run (V12) and the HEAD positive control (V8) are r1 artifacts on code r2 replaced — re-run both on the r2 prototype before quorum.
result.proposed_fix: Add to §7 acceptance, before the CI gate: 'Executor verification (blocking): with the pinned srt install, grep/inspect the proxy's CONNECT handler and record in the sprint Verification Log (a) whether bytes after a 200 are relayed verbatim in both directions, (b) whether any header/banner is prepended or appended upstream. If any alteration exists, the design reverts to fail-at-first-foreign (no retry on windows containing byte-bearing accepts; retry only zero-accept-… no — retry only nothing), i.e. reclassify any accept carrying bytes that begin neither expected line as silent.' Add to §11 round-2 asks: 'Quorum must explicitly ratify R2 as a quantified 1−p³ vs 1−p weakening, not merely note it.' And re-run on the r2 prototype: the −count=3 stability suite (V12's command) and the HEAD positive control (V8's command), appending both as new V rows; r1's results must not stand in for r2 code.
